brief.text:
WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY IT IS SIMPLER

The first pass added instruments to the existing screen. This one takes things away until what is left reads at a glance.

ONE QUESTION PER TILE. Four tiles, each with one figure and one picture: what the shelf is worth (and its 30-day line), how healthy it is (one bar, coloured by state), what runs out inside your cover (crimson), and what has stopped moving (hatched amber). Nothing else stands between the page name and the list.

ONE ROW OF TOOLS. Search, a five-way state filter, category, sort. The filter's dots are the same colours as the health bar above it, so the tile and the filter are one idea.

ONE TABLE, ONE OPEN LINE. Five columns, generous rows, and a cover bar on every row so the eye finds the short bar before it reads a figure. Pressing a row opens it on the right — the big figure is how many days until it is empty, then a three-step ladder (shelf, floor, cover), four figures, sales week by week, and three actions.

GONE: the five-tile strip, the repair banner, the scatter map, the three lanes, the register's five extra columns, the rail of side panels, and three of the six artboards. What they said is either in a tile now or one press away in the open line.

Colour still answers one question each: crimson = running out, amber = caution and dead money, verdigris = healthy, oxide = the one thing to do next. Every value is the app's own tokens, type and components.

CONSIGNMENT. Goods held for others sit on the shelf and can be sold, but they are not your money. So: the value tile shows yours against held as one bar; a Held filter lists the 31 lines; each such row says how many are yours and how many theirs, with the held value beside yours; the open line shows ownership as a bar and offers settling and returning; Movements has a Consignment kind. Nothing held is ever counted in the shelf's value.

NO BARS. Days of cover is a dated pill, "Runs out 13 Sep"; the floor is a ladder of three figures; sales are a week-by-week row of figures with the biggest in bold; a movement's size is its signed figure in a kind-tinted pill; a count's progress is eight dots.

THE DIALOGS. Count the shelf is a count sheet: pick a scope, type what you see, the record fills in the difference and its cost, and only the lines you count are saved. Receive, Correct the count and Change the floor are each one small dialog with one question, one figure that answers it, and one button.
